names.note: The calendar’s own name page for him is «Николай (Виноградов) (другой), протоиерей, сщмч.» — AND THE «(другой)», *another*, IS THE SOURCE’S OWN: the calendar itself marks him off from another man of the same name and surname. The grade, the rank and that parenthetical are stripped and the surname kept; the day line gives only «Сщмч. Николая пресвитера». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns three other folders, so the slug and the display name carry the day, as `nicholas-vinogradov-14-november` and `nicholas-vinogradov-18-november` already do.

death.note: The year the day line closes with, «(1937)», which is the whole of what the source gives; no year of birth anywhere.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 11 декабря ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Николая пресвитера (1937).»

attestations.note: A line of its own, and THE LINE AND THE NAME PAGE ARE ALL THERE IS. The line says «пресвитера» and the name page «протоиерей», archpriest. A FOURTH FOLDER OF THIS NAME, and the hardest of the four to be sure of: the corpus keeps `nicholas-vinogradov` on the Julian 4 ноября with 1931, `nicholas-vinogradov-14-november` on 14 ноября with 1937, and `nicholas-vinogradov-18-november` on 18 ноября with 1948. THIS MAN IS 11 ДЕКАБРЯ WITH 1937, THE SAME YEAR AS THE 14 НОЯБРЯ FOLDER, and the only thing that distinguishes the two is the day — except that the source itself writes «(другой)», another, into his name page, which is the calendar marking him off from a namesake of its own accord. That is why this is a fourth folder and not a second day on an existing one, and it is as far as the reading goes: WHICH namesake the «(другой)» points at is not stated and is not decided here. The day page prints four hymns and none is under his name.
